name: ZeroSevenGroup
iocPatterns: Custom tools for Active Directory hunting
recommendedActions: Implement Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) across all external-facing services and internal legacy systems.
Harden Active Directory environments by auditing permissions and restricting administrative privileges.
Deploy an EDR solution capable of detecting common lateral movement tools like Mimikatz or PlugX.
Perform regular network segmentation between corporate, industrial control systems, and R&D networks.
Implement Data Loss Prevention (DLP) solutions to alert on large outbound data transfers.
Conduct routine vulnerability assessments specifically targeting buffer overflow vulnerabilities in public-facing applications.
Establish a robust incident response plan for 'double extortion' scenarios where both data publication and ransomware are utilized.
Audit third-party access points, as the group has been known to leverage third-party vulnerabilities to compromise primary targets.
campaignsText: ZeroSevenGroup follows a pattern of targeted high-value attacks on multinational corporations and critical infrastructure. Their operations are characterized by slow, deliberate movement within the network to ensure maximum data collection before an 'exit' (exfiltration). They have been observed in campaigns targeting manufacturing (2024 Toyota breach) and energy/infrastructure components. Their timeline suggests a persistent interest in long-term access rather than immediate impact, often resulting in massive data dumps on known leak sites to extort victims.
description: ZeroSevenGroup is a sophisticated, financially motivated cybercriminal threat actor specializing in large-scale data exfiltration and double extortion tactics. They have demonstrated the ability to breach multi-national corporations and critical infrastructure to steal vast amounts of sensitive intellectual property and personal information.
goals: The strategic goals of ZeroSevenGroup are centered on high-value data monetization through theft and extortion. They target sectors with dense intellectual property (manufacturing, mining, nuclear/energy) and critical infrastructure that can be used as leverage in negotiations. By targeting large entities like Toyota or critical Israeli systems, they aim to maximize the visibility of their breaches, thereby increasing the pressure on organizations to pay ransoms while simultaneously selling data on underground forums.
